column1: # PORTVALD parity case table - input side of the parity harness.
# One row per CALL 'PORTVALD'. Expected results are NOT written here: they are captured from the
# compiled COBOL program (see portvald-cobol-golden.tsv and java/run-parity.sh).
# Encoding of validate_type / input_value: \t \n \r \\ and \xHH (one byte, 0x00-0xFF).
#   Values are right-padded with spaces to the COBOL field length (1 and 50); trailing spaces are implicit.
# Categories: VALID, BOUNDARY, FAILURE = expected shapes; QUIRK = executed legacy behaviour that is
#   surprising or contradicts the paragraph's own comment (preserved on purpose, see migration doc).

column5: Unknown validation type 'X' -> WHEN OTHER (rc 1, own message)
Validation type is case-sensitive: lowercase 'i' is not 'I'
Documented-valid format PORT+4 digits is REJECTED: 4 digits moved to PIC X(10) are padded with 6 spaces, which fail IS NUMERIC
PORT followed by 46 digits (field completely full) is still rejected
Trailing bytes after position 8 are never inspected; rejected only by the padding defect
Leading space shifts the prefix out of positions 1-4
Documented-valid 10-digit account is REJECTED: IS NUMERIC tests all 50 bytes and the 40 trailing spaces are not digits
10 zeros rejected by the NUMERIC test (not the ZEROS test)

14 digits: high-order digit truncated -> 0.00, accepted (range check can never fire)

Blank input -> 0.00, accepted (blank treated as zero)
Sign only -> negative zero in GnuCOBOL, accepted
Minus zero -> negative zero in GnuCOBOL, accepted
Second decimal point -> whole value zeroed, accepted
